audit.title: Stream and decode Data Streams reports via WebSocket using the Rust SDK
audit.summary: This is a well-structured, code-complete Rust tutorial that walks the full lifecycle (setup → stream → multi-stream → HA → decode → adapt schemas → verify) with runnable snippets, real endpoint URLs, and inline links to GitHub source lines. Its single biggest GEO strength is code/agent-runnability with authoritative source citations; its single biggest opportunity is machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or last-updated signals in the served markdown) plus the absence of symptom-phrased troubleshooting headings. The honest verdict: strong content that engines can synthesize, but it forfeits easy retrieval/trust lift on metadata and error-query coverage.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom-phrased Troubleshooting section
recommendations.issue: no error-string or failure-phrased headings anywhere on page
recommendations.change: add H3s phrased as errors/questions: "`API_KEY must be set` panic on startup", "Why does HA mode fail on testnet?", "WebSocket connection keeps reconnecting", each with a one-line answer.
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by error string; symptom-titled sections win retrieval that concept prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical, and last-updated
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `programmingLanguage: Rust`, canonical URL, and a visible `dateModified`; surface a "Last updated" line in-page.
recommendations.why: structured metadata + freshness signals raise parse-trust (E-E-A-T) and citation eligibility.

recommendations.title: Fix the WebSocket endpoint inconsistency
recommendations.where: second config snippet under "Set up your API credentials"
recommendations.change: make both snippets use the identical, correct testnet WS URL.
recommendations.why: conflicting specifics get synthesized into wrong endpoints; consistent values prevent hallucinated config.

recommendations.title: Make the HA snippet self-contained
recommendations.issue: `// ... existing code ...` placeholders and no imports
recommendations.change: show the full import line plus the complete `Config::new(...).with_ws_ha(...)` call as a runnable unit, or link to a full gist.
recommendations.why: agents can't assemble elided code; complete blocks are quoted and executed verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add a one-sentence canonical definition of Data Streams near first use
recommendations.issue: "Data Streams Aggregation Network" used without definition
recommendations.change: add a liftable sentence, e.g. "Chainlink Data Streams delivers low-latency, pull-based market data reports verifiable onchain."
recommendations.why: a self-contained definition survives chunking and gets cited verbatim.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifier "robust"
recommendations.where: "Error handling: Uses Rust's `Result` type for robust error handling"
recommendations.change: state the concrete behavior, e.g. "propagates errors with the `?` operator and logs them via `warn!` without crashing the loop."
recommendations.why: specifics outperform qualitative prose in extraction.

antiPatterns: Conflicting endpoint values across two code blocks (WS URL) — accuracy risk for synthesis.
Elided code (`// ... existing code ...`) in the HA snippet — not standalone-runnable.
No stale-date evidence, but also no freshness signal at all (undated content).
offPageNotes: JSON-LD/canonical/`dateModified` are typically site-template-level; fix at the docs platform layer so all tutorials inherit them.
`llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good; ensure this page is listed in it and in the sitemap.
Earned citations (third-party Rust/Chainlink tutorials linking here) are off-page and not scored, but would raise retrieval rank.
